pairs.why: B has the soft light glow behind a bright cream-edged stack that separates by value from the pink, like the real card, while A is a darker, flatter magenta with a tan hero that has less value gap.
B's black engine sits against a large bright sky so it separates by value, as in the real cards' bright mid-key; A's black mass merges with dark rails and a busy brown ground.
Both have the same key, the same bright rays and the same grey ground with a white hero, so value gives no reason to choose.
A's larger, glowing orange glass with bright ice reads as a bright hero against a mid purple, closer to the real card, while B is smaller with a darker, heavier background and ground shadow.
Both match the real card's bright cyan rings, warm canopy and dark red underside, so value gives no reason to prefer one.
B keeps the keys dark navy and low-contrast within the dark body, as in the real card, while A's pale grey keys add a bright local-contrast pop the real card lacks.
B has a lighter pale floor and softer, gentler local contrast like the real card, while A has more saturated, harder dark and light accents.
B has darker green stripes toward the corners and a drop shadow beside the clock, like the real card's vignette, while A is flat high-key with a light floor band.
